changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For buyers who come in already losing orders at checkout: Find out why your orders are dying at the last step, especially on the big baskets, and what those lost orders are worth to you. Lead with a diagnosis of the prospect's own declines from their own data (for example, a three-month decline export) instead of the average uplift. Use 'orders dying at the last step' and 'the big baskets' in place of 'authorization rates'.
changes.why: The specific explanation of why big orders fail landed with the champion, while the average-uplift slide was shown and the decider still saw 'the same thing'.

changes.change: For champions who carry the deal to a CFO we can't meet: a one-page business case they can hand the decider. It puts their own failed-order rate, what those failed orders are worth, and our price side by side, written for someone who never saw the demo. Offer it before pricing goes to finance.
changes.why: The champion asked for 'a one-page business case' to hand the CFO, got the deck and pricing instead, and the decision was made on a controller's rate-only one-pager where our only input was the quote.

changes.change: When an incumbent bank counters on rate, answer with the cost of failed orders, not a counter-rate. A lower rate on orders that still fail at checkout doesn't fix the problem you came to us with. Keep the conversation on why big orders fail and what that costs.
changes.why: Before the bank sharpened its rate the champion was asking about declines, after it 'every email was the rate', and nothing shows the bank ever explained the failing orders.
